Array.prototype.push is inherited from the builtin Array prototype, not an own property of the result array; the ResultArray shape covers only the own length slot and builtin prototype chains are not expressible, so the method load stays generic.

Loose comparison against null of a SplayTree.Node-or-null call result (find / findGreatestLessThan). The type language can express null/undefined but has no object type for the non-null branch, and a null|undefined guard on the result was verified to have no effect, so the test stays generic.

String concatenation ('Key not found: ' + key) building the Error argument on the throw path. Both a string type guard on the concat expression and a number type guard on key were added and verified by checklist query to leave this arithmetic generic, so it cannot be specialized.

Date - Date on the timing values and the resulting Time: + number concatenation. Date objects are not expressible in the type language (no object type; subtraction goes through generic ToPrimitive/valueOf dispatch), and the concat depends on that generic result, so neither operation can be specialized.
